hook: A pond at the edge of a farm looks like one thing, but it is thousands of living things and the water, light and mud they depend on. Frogs eat insects, insects eat algae, and a single cold spring can change all of it. To predict what happens when anything changes, you first need words for the parts and for how species affect each other.

figure.caption: How two species can affect each other: + helped, − harmed, 0 not affected.

chain.cause: Two species need the same limited resource
chain.effect: each gets less, so both are harmed: competition

chain.cause: They split the resource by place, time or food size

chain.effect: both species can live in the same community

ideas: An ecosystem is the living (biotic) and nonliving (abiotic) parts of an area and how they interact.
A population is one species in one area; a community is every population living and interacting there.
A habitat is where a species lives; its niche is its role: what it eats, when, where and under what conditions.
Symbiosis is a close, long-term relationship: mutualism (+/+), commensalism (+/0), parasitism (+/−). Predation is +/−, competition is −/−.

misconception.wrong: Any relationship where one species eats part of another is predation.
misconception.right: A predator kills and eats its prey. A parasite lives on or in a host for a long time and harms it, usually without killing it right away. Ask: does the host stay alive while it is fed on?

summary: An ecosystem joins a community of species to the abiotic conditions around it. Species interact by predation (+/−), competition (−/−) and three kinds of symbiosis: mutualism (+/+), commensalism (+/0) and parasitism (+/−). Species that need the same resource can still coexist by resource partitioning, using it at different places or times.
